title: Orbital Mechanics: Kepler's Laws & Gravitational Escape Dynamics
pedagogical_goal: Demonstrate how a planet orbits a central star, showing conservation of angular momentum (equal areas swept in equal times), velocity changes at periapsis vs apoapsis, and escape velocity threshold.

conservation_laws: Newton's Law of Universal Gravitation: F = G * M * m / r^2
Conservation of Angular Momentum: L = m * r * v_perp = Constant
Escape Velocity: v_esc = sqrt(2 * G * M / r)

components.description: Central star located at the focal point of the elliptical orbit, with radiant multi-layer corona pulse.
Precise mathematical ellipse showing the orbital trajectory with dashed grid markings.
Planet orbiting according to Kepler's 2nd Law (moving fastest at periapsis and slowest at apoapsis), leaving a glowing fading particle tail.
Real-time velocity vector (tangent to orbit) and gravitational acceleration vector (pointing directly at central star).
Kinetic Energy vs Gravitational Potential Energy exchange showing negative total mechanical energy for bound orbits.

pedagogical_callouts.title: 1. Kepler's First Law
pedagogical_callouts.text: Planets move in elliptical orbits with the central star situated at one of the two foci, not at the center.

pedagogical_callouts.title: 2. Equal Areas in Equal Times
pedagogical_callouts.text: As the planet nears periapsis (closest approach), gravitational pull intensifies, accelerating the planet to maximum speed.

pedagogical_callouts.title: 3. The Escape Boundary
pedagogical_callouts.text: If tangential speed exceeds the escape velocity threshold, total mechanical energy becomes positive, transforming the ellipse into a hyperbolic escape trajectory!
